items.title: The sign of Entropy Change and Spontaneity of a Process

source_refs.note: The sign of Entropy Change and Spontaneity of a Process: a main subheading of 6.11.3 Entropy changes in reactions, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 138-138.

blocks.text: The entropy of a substance is always positive, however, when the entropy changes it may have positive or negative value.
A positive entropy change value (ΔS° = +ve) means a spontaneous process
A negative entropy change value(ΔS° = -ve) implies more ordered molecules and a decrease in disorder
For some reactions, however, the entropy change fails to tell about the spontaneity of the reaction and we need another quantity called free energy.

blocks.title: Quick Check 6.9
blocks.text:
a) What do you expect about the entropy value of the following reactions, whether it would be positive or negative?
i) N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g)
ii) 2HI(g) → H₂(g) + I₂(g)
b) Which of the following changes are likely to be spontaneous?
i. The smell from an open bottle of aqueous ammonia diffusing throughout a room
ii. Water turning to ice at -10 °c
iii. Ethanol vaporising at 20 °c
iv. Water mixing completely with salt
v. Limestone (calcium carbonate) decomposing at room temperature
